authoring_notes: This tree is based on ranked in-house experience for Prusa Core One plus generic FDM troubleshooting coverage.
Lower rank number means more likely cause.
Keep node IDs stable once the frontend depends on them.
All question options must point to an existing node ID.

q_filament_not_sticking_1.text: Is the print bed visibly dirty, greasy, or covered with old glue residue?
q_filament_not_sticking_1.help_text: On Core One printers, a dirty plate is one of the most common causes of poor first-layer adhesion.

q_filament_not_sticking_2.text: Does the first layer look too high, with poor squish or gaps between lines?
q_filament_not_sticking_2.help_text: Watch the first layer closely. Poor squish usually points to a bed/nozzle gap issue.

q_filament_not_sticking_3.text: Has the nozzle been cleaned recently before recalibration?

d_filament_not_sticking_dirty_bed.label: Dirty Bed
d_filament_not_sticking_dirty_bed.description: The build plate likely has grease, dust, or adhesive buildup preventing adhesion.

d_filament_not_sticking_z_offset_high.label: Print Head Too Far From Bed
d_filament_not_sticking_z_offset_high.description: First-layer calibration likely failed or the nozzle is too far from the bed.
likely_causes: Print head too far from bed (failed calibration)

d_filament_not_sticking_clean_nozzle.label: Nozzle Debris Affecting First Layer
d_filament_not_sticking_clean_nozzle.description: Debris on the nozzle can interfere with probing or first-layer consistency.

d_filament_not_sticking_run_calibration.label: Re-run First Layer Calibration
d_filament_not_sticking_run_calibration.description: No obvious contamination found. Re-run first-layer calibration and inspect plate condition again.

q_filament_not_extruding_1.text: Is filament currently loaded into the printer?
q_filament_not_extruding_1.help_text: Start with the most common and least invasive checks first.

q_filament_not_extruding_2.text: Is filament present at the extruder entrance when the tube is disconnected or inspected?

q_filament_not_extruding_3.text: Is the filament broken or stuck inside the extruder path?

q_filament_not_extruding_4.text: When the nozzle is hot, can filament be pushed through manually?
q_filament_not_extruding_4.help_text: If it cannot be pushed through a hot nozzle, treat it as a clog branch first.

d_filament_not_extruding_not_loaded.label: No Filament Loaded
d_filament_not_extruding_not_loaded.description: The printer has no filament loaded.

d_filament_not_extruding_not_in_extruder.label: Filament Not Reaching Extruder
d_filament_not_extruding_not_in_extruder.description: Filament is not actually entering the extruder feed path.
recommended_actions: Load filament from tube to extruder

d_filament_not_extruding_broken_filament.label: Broken Filament In Extruder
d_filament_not_extruding_broken_filament.description: Filament has snapped inside the extruder path.
recommended_actions: Open filament idler and remove filament

d_filament_not_extruding_nozzle_clog.label: Filament Clogged In Nozzle
d_filament_not_extruding_nozzle_clog.description: The nozzle is likely clogged and blocking flow.
recommended_actions: Pick filament out of nozzle after heating

d_filament_not_extruding_feed_issue.label: Extruder Feed Issue
d_filament_not_extruding_feed_issue.description: The nozzle appears open enough for manual push, so focus on loading or feeder grip issues.

q_under_extrusion_1.text: Is there visible debris or partial blockage at the nozzle tip or in extrusion quality?
q_under_extrusion_1.help_text: Your ranking puts nozzle debris as the most likely cause.

q_under_extrusion_2.text: Does extrusion improve when nozzle temperature is increased slightly within the filament range?

d_under_extrusion_debris_nozzle.label: Debris In Nozzle
d_under_extrusion_debris_nozzle.description: A partial blockage or debris in the nozzle is the most likely cause.

d_under_extrusion_low_temp.label: Nozzle Temperature Too Low
d_under_extrusion_low_temp.description: If extrusion improves with more heat, the nozzle may be too cold for the filament/material state.

d_under_extrusion_general_path_check.label: General Filament Path Restriction
d_under_extrusion_general_path_check.description: If it is not clearly temperature-related, inspect the broader filament path and feeder.

q_layer_shift_1.text: Is the chamber unusually hot or poorly ventilated during the print?
q_layer_shift_1.help_text: Your ranking puts high chamber temperature first.

q_layer_shift_2.text: Was the print running unusually fast for the model or material?

q_layer_shift_3.text: Are supports missing or are curled-up features crashing into the nozzle?

q_layer_shift_4.text: Do belts feel loose or overly tight when checked manually?
q_layer_shift_4.help_text: Incorrect belt tension is a common mechanical cause of shifting.

d_layer_shift_hot_chamber.label: High Chamber Temperature
d_layer_shift_hot_chamber.description: Excessive chamber heat may contribute to print issues that lead to shifts or collisions.

d_layer_shift_print_too_fast.label: Print Too Fast
d_layer_shift_print_too_fast.description: Motion stability or cooling may be inadequate at the current speed.

d_layer_shift_supports.label: Insufficient Supports / Curling Features
d_layer_shift_supports.description: A curled feature or unsupported overhang may have been hit by the nozzle.

d_layer_shift_belt_tension.label: Incorrect Belt Tension
d_layer_shift_belt_tension.description: Belts may be too loose or too tight, causing skipped or inaccurate motion.
recommended_actions: Tighten or loosen belt to correct tension

d_layer_shift_overlap_or_overextrusion.label: Model Overlap / Over-Extrusion Check
d_layer_shift_overlap_or_overextrusion.description: If the usual mechanical checks are okay, inspect the slice for overlap or abnormal over-extrusion conditions.

q_bed_level_fail_1.text: Is the bed seated correctly and placed in the correct position?
q_bed_level_fail_1.help_text: Check the simplest mechanical mistake first.

q_bed_level_fail_2.text: Is there debris on the bed surface?

q_bed_level_fail_3.text: Is there debris on the nozzle tip that could affect probing or first layer sensing?

d_bed_level_fail_bed_position.label: Incorrectly Placed Bed
d_bed_level_fail_bed_position.description: The bed may not be seated or positioned correctly.

d_bed_level_fail_debris_bed.label: Debris On Bed
d_bed_level_fail_debris_bed.description: Surface debris is interfering with bed leveling or first layer setup.

d_bed_level_fail_debris_nozzle.label: Debris On Nozzle
d_bed_level_fail_debris_nozzle.description: Debris on the nozzle can cause false offsets or bad calibration.

d_bed_level_fail_unleveled_bed.label: Bed Needs Manual Reset / Re-Level
d_bed_level_fail_unleveled_bed.description: If bed and nozzle are clean and positioned correctly, reset and manually level the bed.
recommended_actions: Disable stepper and manually screw bed all the way to bottom

q_unable_change_filament_1.text: Is the filament physically unable to pull out from the hotend side during unload?
q_unable_change_filament_1.help_text: Start with the least invasive recovery method.

q_unable_change_filament_2.text: Has the filament broken inside the tube?

q_unable_change_filament_3.text: Is the filament stuck inside the nozzle/hotend?

d_unable_change_filament_pull_both_sides.label: Filament Unable To Pull Out
d_unable_change_filament_pull_both_sides.description: The filament is stuck but may still be freed by controlled pulling from accessible sides.

d_unable_change_filament_broken_tube.label: Filament Broke In Tube
d_unable_change_filament_broken_tube.description: A broken piece remains trapped in the tube/path.
recommended_actions: Feed filament from one side, and push broken filament out from the other side
d_unable_change_filament_broken_tube.fix_summary: Pushed broken filament out of tube

d_unable_change_filament_stuck_nozzle.label: Filament Stuck Inside Nozzle
d_unable_change_filament_stuck_nozzle.description: The material is jammed inside the nozzle or hotend.
recommended_actions: Take nozzle out and clean filament out with heated air gun

d_unable_change_filament_feeder_issue.label: Filament Feeder Obstruction
d_unable_change_filament_feeder_issue.description: If tube and nozzle paths are not the issue, open the feeder and inspect the path.
likely_causes: Filament unable to feed into tube

q_fan_not_spinning_1.text: Is there visible debris blocking the fan blades?

q_fan_not_spinning_2.text: Is the fan cable disconnected or loose at the board/fan end?

d_fan_not_spinning_debris.label: Debris In Fan
d_fan_not_spinning_debris.description: Debris is preventing the fan from rotating properly.

d_fan_not_spinning_cable.label: Fan Cable Disconnected
d_fan_not_spinning_cable.description: The fan connection may be loose or disconnected.

d_fan_not_spinning_broken.label: Fan Failed
d_fan_not_spinning_broken.description: If it is clean and connected but still not spinning, the fan is likely faulty.

sop_clean_bed_ipa.title: Clean Bed With IPA
sop_clean_bed_ipa.description: Wipe the build surface thoroughly with IPA and a lint-free cloth.

sop_clean_nozzle_tip.title: Clean Nozzle Tip
sop_clean_nozzle_tip.description: Remove debris from the nozzle tip safely before calibration or printing.

sop_first_layer_calibration.title: First Layer Calibration
sop_first_layer_calibration.description: Check bed condition and run first-layer or Z-offset calibration.

sop_load_filament.title: Load Filament
sop_load_filament.description: Load filament correctly through the feeder and extruder path.

sop_feed_filament_to_extruder.title: Feed Filament To Extruder
sop_feed_filament_to_extruder.description: Guide filament from PTFE path or inlet into the extruder correctly.

sop_open_idler_remove_filament.title: Open Idler And Remove Filament
sop_open_idler_remove_filament.description: Open the idler and remove broken or jammed filament safely.

sop_nozzle_needle_clean.title: Needle Clean Nozzle
sop_nozzle_needle_clean.description: Heat appropriately and use a nozzle needle to clear a simple blockage.

sop_cold_pull.title: Cold Pull Procedure
sop_cold_pull.description: Perform a cold pull to remove internal debris from the hotend.

sop_raise_nozzle_temp.title: Raise Nozzle Temperature
sop_raise_nozzle_temp.description: Increase nozzle temperature within material-safe range and re-test extrusion.

sop_chamber_fan_on.title: Turn On Chamber Fan
sop_chamber_fan_on.description: Enable chamber ventilation to reduce internal temperature.

sop_reduce_print_speed.title: Reduce Print Speed
sop_reduce_print_speed.description: Lower print speed and re-test for stability.

sop_add_supports.title: Re-slice With Supports
sop_add_supports.description: Add adequate supports and re-slice the model.

sop_adjust_belt_tension.title: Adjust Belt Tension
sop_adjust_belt_tension.description: Check and correct belt tension without overtightening.

sop_check_model_overlap.title: Check Model Overlap / Over-Extrusion
sop_check_model_overlap.description: Inspect slice for overlapping objects or abnormal flow conditions.

sop_correct_bed_position.title: Correct Bed Position
sop_correct_bed_position.description: Re-seat the bed correctly before leveling.

sop_manual_bed_level.title: Manual Bed Level Reset
sop_manual_bed_level.description: Disable steppers and manually reset/level the bed.

sop_pull_filament_both_sides.title: Pull Filament From Both Sides
sop_pull_filament_both_sides.description: Free filament by pulling gently from accessible sides.

sop_push_broken_filament_out.title: Push Broken Filament Out
sop_push_broken_filament_out.description: Use intact filament from one side to push the broken piece through.

sop_hot_air_clean_nozzle.title: Hot Air Clean Nozzle
sop_hot_air_clean_nozzle.description: Remove nozzle and clear stuck filament using hot air carefully.

sop_disassemble_feeder.title: Disassemble Filament Feeder
sop_disassemble_feeder.description: Open the feeder to clear path issues preventing filament insertion.

sop_clean_fan.title: Clean Fan Debris
sop_clean_fan.description: Remove debris preventing the fan from spinning freely.

sop_reconnect_fan_cable.title: Reconnect Fan Cable
sop_reconnect_fan_cable.description: Inspect board and fan connection, then reconnect securely.

sop_replace_fan.title: Replace Fan
sop_replace_fan.description: Swap failed fan with a known-good replacement.

shortcuts_hint: Use diagnosis result fields to prefill manual reactive maintenance logging.
Diagnosis node 'fix_summary' is suitable for dashboard summary text.
